methodology: To decompose the original research topic and the generated technical specification into atomic units, I systematically analyzed both texts to identify distinct requirements, features, behaviors, and constraints. Each atomic unit was defined as an independent and self-contained statement that is technically specific and unambiguous. I focused on extracting individual actions, conditions, and outputs related to the Lemmings' behavior in the finite state machine model. This involved breaking down complex sentences into simpler components while ensuring that each unit could stand alone as a requirement. I also ensured that the units from both sources were comparable in terms of their specificity and independence.
mindtraced_atomic_units: Lemmings can be in one of two states: walking left or walking right.
Lemmings switch directions if they hit an obstacle.
A bump on the left makes a Lemming walk right.
A bump on the right makes a Lemming walk left.
If bumped on both sides simultaneously, the Lemming switches directions.
When ground = 0, the Lemming falls and says 'aaah!'.
When ground = 1, the Lemming resumes walking in the same direction as before the fall.
Being bumped while falling does not affect walking direction.
Bumps in the same cycle as ground transitions do not affect walking direction.
Lemmings can dig when ground = 1 and not falling.
A Lemming continues digging until it reaches ground = 0.
When reaching ground = 0, the Lemming falls and resumes walking in its original direction.
Being bumped while digging has no effect.
Dig commands while falling or without ground are ignored.
The precedence of actions is: falling > digging > switching directions.
Implement a Moore state machine to model this behavior.
The areset signal triggers an asynchronous reset to walk left.
spec_atomic_units: The module 'top_module' implements a Moore finite state machine to model Lemmings' behavior.
Lemmings can walk left or right.
Lemmings switch directions upon receiving bumps.
Lemmings fall when there is no ground.
Lemmings can dig when on the ground.
The module has inputs for clock, asynchronous reset, bump signals, ground status, and dig command.
The outputs indicate walking direction, falling state, and digging status.
The 'clk' input triggers state transitions on the positive edge.
The 'areset' input asynchronously resets the state machine to walking left.
The 'bump_left' and 'bump_right' inputs affect walking direction.
The 'ground' input determines if the Lemming is falling or walking.
The 'dig' input allows the Lemming to dig when on the ground.
State transitions occur on the positive edge of 'clk'.
The 'areset' signal has priority and resets the state immediately.
The 'ground' input must be stable for at least one clock cycle before affecting the state.
Non-blocking assignments are used for state updates.
